configuration.enablement: The `DOC` prefix is part of the default selection, so selection alone cannot express opt-in: each documentation rule stays inert until `enabled = true` is set under `[tool.stilyagi.rule.CODE]`. `lint.ignore`, a matching `lint.per-file-ignores` entry, or removing `builtin` from `plugins` removes the rule from the enabled set before it runs; a `stilyagi: disable` directive instead suppresses reported findings after evaluation.

constraints: The rule stays inert, reporting nothing, until this is true.
options.description: Whether the rule may report for this configuration.
options.name: enabled

variants.description: Keep the rule inert even though `DOC` selects it.
Let the rule report on the regions it claims.

rule.explanation: A Python docstring's first content line is its summary. When a further line follows it with no blank line between them, the summary and the explanation run together, which most renderers show as one paragraph. Only Python docstrings are inspected; Rust documentation comments, Markdown, and ordinary comments are not.
rule.fixes: The rule offers no fix. Rewriting a summary is editorial, so no edit is planned and `--fix` leaves the source unchanged.
limitations: One-line docstrings, docstrings whose summary is the only content, and regions whose source span cannot be located are not reported.
Configuration, per-file ignores, and suppression directives can stop a finding; static metadata does not describe effective enablement for a particular file.
rule.name: summary-separation
rule.summary: Report a Python docstring summary with no blank separator line.
